Nestled within the intricate maze of Hanoi’s historic 36 Old Streets, Ma May Street unfolds like a slow-moving film, capturing the vibrant essence of the capital city’s dynamic life. Historically, this street emerged from the fusion of two ancient alleys: Hang Ma, known for its trade in religious paraphernalia such as paper offerings and incense, and Hang May, renowned for its sales of rattan straps and woven bamboo and rattan products.

The architectural landscape of Ma May Street is dominated by the traditional tube houses, each a testament to the region’s vernacular building techniques. These elongated structures, typically no more than three meters wide but extending deep into the block, are constructed primarily from wood and brick, with intricate lattice windows and ornamental doorways that allow natural light to filter through while maintaining privacy.

The juxtaposition of these timeless buildings against the backdrop of modern neon lights creates a visually striking contrast, drawing the eye and inviting exploration. Cultural significance permeates every corner of Ma May Street, making it a vital part of Hanoi’s cultural heritage.
